messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: INC-2026-034: elevated error rate and streaming stalls for hosted inference. Affected path: streaming + continuous-batcher + KV cache paging. Auto-alerting to #incidents and oncall.

Alice_oncall: Ack. I'm looking at the dashboards now. Latency spikes at ~08:12 UTC, error rate on streaming endpoints + partial token flushes reported.

Bob_sre: Seeing KVCache memory graph — unusual growth starting 08:10, then GC thrash. Looks like paging loop causing repeated cache pinning for very long contexts.

Cheng_ml: Correlating with continuous batching change we rolled last night (batch.max_inflight = 48, batch.prefix_cache_enabled = true). Could be amplification: large batch sizes + aggressive prefix caching + paging = cache blowup.

Diego_runtime: Logs show repeated page-loads for same doc keys. Example error snippet:
```
[08:11:34] KVCache WARN: exceeded_capacity key_count=124567 capacity=100k action=block_until_free
[08:11:35] ContinuousBatcher ERROR: stall_detected last_token_delta_ms=412 stall_count=3 route=streaming/model-x
```

Alice_oncall: Temporary mitigation idea: reduce batch.max_inflight to 8 and disable prefix_cache for streaming routes. That should reduce simultaneous memory pressure and stop the repeated page fetches.

Bob_sre: Agreed. Creating a quick hotfix. Will push config change to prod via deploy-bot.

Deploy-bot: Starting config rollout: set batch.max_inflight=8 for service=runtime-streaming, set batch.prefix_cache_enabled=false for route=streaming/*. Rolling: zone-a -> zone-b -> zone-c.

Erin_support: Customer impact — Support ticket count up 3x. Customers report token stalls (generative responses stop mid-stream for ~5-10s then resume partial). No known data loss. Notifying top 5 enterprise customers.

Diego_runtime: Applying runtime patch to evict oversized page sets faster (kv.page_eviction_threshold=0.6 -> 0.4) and added safeguard to prevent re-pinning same page within 30s. Pushing patch to canary now.

Alice_oncall: Canary looks good for 3 minutes. Memory usage in canary halved and batch latency back to baseline. Rolling to remaining zones.

Bob_sre: After rollout, errors dropped ~93% and continuous-batcher stall alerts cleared. Streaming latency still a hair higher for long contexts but stable.

Cheng_ml: Root cause hypothesis: combination of increased inflight batches + prefix caching allowed many pages to be loaded and pinned concurrently; a paging edge-case re-requested the same page on eviction which caused thrashing and cache growth. Continuous batcher then experienced token cadence stalls when KV lookups delayed token emission.

Erin_support: Logged customer-facing summary and outreach. Marking impacted customers and adding an inbound note to the P1 ticket.

Alice_oncall: Severity lowered to P2 at 08:40 UTC. I'll start a postmortem runbook and hand off to morning oncall.

Bob_sre: Creating follow-up tasks:
- Add a safety cap: batch.max_inflight upper limit per-route (task#INC-2026-034-1)
- Add re-pin debounce on KV paging (task#INC-2026-034-2)
- Increase observability: per-doc page load counters, per-request page fetch latency (task#INC-2026-034-3)

Diego_runtime: Also adding a streaming-specific config that disables prefix cache for routes with dynamic paging. Should reduce risk of reintroducing this pattern.

Alice_oncall: Handoff to @bob_sre for daytime follow-up. Summary for next oncall: hotfix rolled (batch.max_inflight=8, prefix_cache disabled on streaming), kv eviction threshold lowered, canary pass, severity P2. Watch for recurrence in next 24h and slow-roll config re-enables only after 72h with safety metrics.

Bob_sre: Taking handoff. I'll coordinate postmortem and schedule a small rollback test for staging.

Erin_support: Closing immediate customer comms loop; will append timeline in support cases.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-034 status -> mitigated (P2). Postmortem requested: owner=bob_sre; due=2026-03-20.

Alice_oncall: Quick notes for postmortem: include exact commit SHAs for last-night batching change, timeline of KV cache growth, paging telemetry, and decision trail to hotfix. Also include suggested automated guardrails for batch config changes.

Bob_sre: Will write draft and loop in runtime, ML infra, and support. Thanks all. :white_check_mark: :eyes:
